P009653.project_abstract: The Andhra Pradesh Agricultural Credit Project will finance an investment program in minor irrigation, land levelling and farm mechanization in the State of Andhra Pradesh. It will be part of a continuing program of support by the Association to the Government of India and to the State Governments to further their policies to expand credit facilities to farmers and thus to assist them in taking advantage of modern methods of cultivation through necessary on-farm investments. It will increase minor irrigation facilities in the State by the installation of some 1,350 tubewells and 14,000 dugwells, and by the improvement of some 5,000 existing dugwells. In addition almost 20,000 pump sets will be financed for installation in existing wells or wells to be developed under the project. The purchase of some 1,500 tractors with some implement components will also be financed. In addition to the lending program there is provision for consultancy services to a State Ground Water Directorate to be established and for a study of the procedures of one of the lending institutions - the LMB.

P009652.project_abstract: The Agricultural Aviation Project will support a program of aerial spraying which began in 1957 and will complement other IDA assistance to India in the agricultural sector. It will form an important part of India's plant protection program for the current Five-Year Plan period (1969-1974), by providing finance for the foreign exchange costs of: (a) about 82 agricultural aircraft (67 for the use of qualified private operators and 15 for the GOI Directorate of Agricultural Aviation); (b) spare parts and ancillary equipment; and (c) training agricultural pilots and engineers. Purchase of aircraft by private operators will be through a credit program to be run by ARC.

P009647.project_abstract: The Punjab Agricultural Credit Project will help finance a program for farm mechanization including tractors, harvesters and farm implements.

P009649.project_abstract: The Eighth Industrial Credit Project will finance the foreign exchange cost of investment projects carried out by productive enterprises in India.

P009646.project_abstract: This project includes: (a) provision of long-term finance: (i) to farmers in the project area for investments in minor irrigation equipment and facilities, specifically: the installation of pump sets for existing wells; construction of new open wells complete with pump sets; installation of shallow and dug tubewells; construction of lift irrigation schemes; laying of pipelines; and lining of distributaries and field channels and electrification for installations financed as above; (ii) to farmers for the purchase of tractors, tractor implements and harvesters; and (iii) to contractors for the purchase of drilling rigs, including necessary ancillary equipment and spare parts; (b) a study of the general water resources and potential for development in the project area.

P009650.project_abstract: The Sixth Industrial Imports Project will enable selected priority industries in India to maintain and expand their production of capital goods and agricultural chemicals by supplying part of their requirements of foreign exchange for the import of materials, components and spare parts.

P009648.project_abstract: The project includes: (a) construction of the Kadana Dam on the Mahi River; (b) expansion of the existing irrigation system on the right bank from 143,000 ha to 263,000 ha; (c) construction of a new irrigation system on the left bank to serve about 20,000 ha; (d) construction of watercourses and field channels throughout the project area; (e) remodeling and expansion of the drainage systems; (f) land leveling of about 42,000 ha; and (g) upgrading of existing roads and construction of new district village and farm-to-market roads totaling about 3,200 km. It also includes groundwater investigations, a study of water charges, a trial land consolidation program and construction of trial-cum-demonstration farms.

P009651.project_abstract: The planned investments during the two-year project period, April 1, 1969 to March 31, 1971, will aggregate the equivalent of US$709 million; about 44% of the total will be for rolling stock and about 16% will represent line capacity work such as double tracing and gauge conversion. The foreign exchange component will be about US$95 million equivalent, and represents the cost of imported equipment and of imported components for equipment manufactured in the Railways' workshops. The local currency cost of the project will be financed by the Railways and from the central government budget. Apart from the proceeds of the proposed credit, foreign exchange requirements are to be obtained bilaterally, and from India's own resources. The import of components and materials for rolling stock comprise the largest single category under the proposed credit (69%); other important items will be for the import of electrical equipment and for signalling and telecommunications.

P009644.project_abstract: The project which the Third Telecommunications Project will help finance is a three year (1969/70-1971/72) portion of the telecommunications investment program. The total capital expenditure target for the three year period is US$361 million, of which about US$103 million (less than 30 percent) will be required in foreign exchange. About half of this will be used to import microwave equipment, coaxial cable equipment and telephone cable, and the balance to import materials and components for local manufacture of switching and transmission equipment, telephones, teleprinters and cable.

P009643.project_abstract: The Terai Seeds Project will finance on-farm improvements, installation of seed processing plants, and other developments necessary for production of certified seeds of high-yielding varieties of foodgrains.

P009645.project_abstract: The Fifth Industrial Imports Project will enable selected priority industries in India to maintain and expand their production of capital goods and agricultural chemicals by financing part of their requirements of foreign exchange for the import of raw materials, components, spare parts and miscellaneous items of manufacturing equipment. The foreign exchange is sold by the Government of India to the ultimate beneficiaries.

P009642.project_abstract: The Seventh Industrial Credit Project will assist in meeting the foreign exchange costs of projects to be financed by ICICI.

P009640.project_abstract: The proposed credit would improve the rate of utilization of existing productive capacity and capital equipment in India by increasing the availability of foreign exchange for the import of materials, components, spare parts and miscellaneous items of manufacturing equipment.

P009639.project_abstract: The proposed project would help finance a program designed to increase IISCO's primary steel-making capacity, to improve the utilization of existing rolling mills and finishing lines, and to provide essential imported spare and replacement parts.

P009638.project_abstract: The proposed credit would finance part of the foreign exchange expenditure of the Railways' investment program during the period from December 1, 1965 to December 31, 1966.

P009636.project_abstract: The project forms a part of a program to increase the utilization of existing manufacturing capacity and provides primarily for the import of materials, components and spare parts required by manufacturers of road transport equipment (trucks, buses, engines and automotive components), electrical equipment (including cables and wires), machine tools, cutting tools and construction equipment. In addition to the foreign exchange which would be provided from proceeds of the proposed IDA credit an equivalent amount will be allocated to these same industries from other sources of foreign exchange available to the Government of India.

P009634.project_abstract: The proposed loan will continue assisting the Andhra Pradesh State Electricity Board by financing the foreign exchange cost of extending the Kothagudem thermal station to a capacity of 240 MW.

P009633.project_abstract: The proposed loan would assist in the extension and interconnection of electric power transmission facilities throughout India by financing the imported equipment and materials required to complete approximately 8,000 miles of high voltage lines and about 300 sub-stations.

P009632.project_abstract: The Sixth Industrial Credit Project will help the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India Limited to continue its foreign exchange assistance to private industrial enterprises in India.

P009635.project_abstract: The major part of the proposed credit would finance the import of steel and components for steam and electric locomotives, electric multiple units, coaches, bogie wagons and signalling equipment, together with equipment and materials for the electrification program. The total foreign exchange requirements of the railways during the period covered by the proposed credit are estimated at around $141 million, and the remaining $79 million would be almost entirely financed under bilateral aid from other members of the Indian Consortium.

P009631.project_abstract: The Second Telecommunications Project in India will assist in financing the program for the rehabilitation, modernization and expansion of telecommunications facilities. This project will cover the estimated cost of importing raw materials and components required by The Indian Post and Telegraphs Department (P&T) and the three principal manufacturers of telecommunications equipment to meet the needs of the program. This project will provide; imports of raw materials, components, minor machinery and test equipment used in P&T workshops.

P009630.project_abstract: The Industrial Imports Project in India will finance a portion of the foreign exchange requirements of industries producing capital goods in India. This project will consist of foreign exchange to cover part of the cost of components, materials and balancing equipment for factories producing trucks, buses and commercial vehicle engines, construction equipment (such as shovels and cranes), machine tools, heavy electrical equipment (including switchgear, motors, transformers, etc.), cutting tools and similar items of capital equipment. In addition, a portion of the credit will be used to import construction equipment, and spare parts required to help maintain India's present stock of commercial vehicles and heavy construction. This project will provide components, materials, and individual pieces of equipment to a wide variety of private sector industries.

P009625.project_abstract: The Fifth Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) Project in India will finance a loan to replenish its foreign exchange resources. This project will encourage local and foreign private capital participation, and assist in the expansion of the Indian capital market. It will consist of two rupee loans from the Government of India. This project will assist in the development of private industry, and encourage local and foreign private capital participation.

P009627.project_abstract: The Kothagudem Power Project in India will help finance a thermal power project will consist of a new 120 MW steam power station near Kothagudem, a reservoir to provide make-up water for the cooling towers of the station, and some transmission facilities. Power demand in Andhra Pradesh has grown at a fast rate. Due to insufficient generating capacity, there has been an acute shortage of power. This proposed project is urgently needed to improve the situation.

P009629.project_abstract: The Seventh Railways Project in India will finance the foreign exchange requirements for the development of the third five-year plan. This project will consist of buying components, and materials used in the manufacture of locomotives, and rolling stock in India. It will also finance equipment for the electrification program, track, and other materials and equipment. This project will provide further development of the Indian economy.

P009628.project_abstract: The Bombay Port Project in India will finance the development program. The projects main objective will provide additional capacity to cope with present and future traffic, particularly at the principal facility the Alexandra dock. Present facilities are inadequate to cope with existing traffic and the project is also essential to provide accommodation for the expected growth in traffic during the next few years. This project will eliminate congestion and materially assist in the economic development for India.

P009624.project_abstract: The Telecommunications Project in India will assist in financing the program for rehabilitation, modernization and expansion of telecommunications facilities. This program will modernize and expand the telephone and telegraph facilities throughout India, and will be carried out by the posts and telegraphs department. The project will expand the telephone and telegraph facilities, and improve the quality of the service.

P009626.project_abstract: The Second Koyna Hydroelectric Project in India will provide financing for the hydroelectric project, south east of Bombay in the state of Maharashtra. The Koyna development will be carried out in three stages: Stage I, will provide capacity of 240 MW; Stage II, will add 340 MW; and Stage III, will provide 100 MW in a tailwater plant. This project will consists of: (a) raising the height of the dam from elevation 2, 107 feet to its designed height of 2,180 feet; (b) completing the Koyna underground power station and installing four 75 MW Pelton type turbo-generating sets with transformer equipment, (c) constructing a small power station at the base of Koyna dam with two Kaplan type turbo - generating units of 20 MW each; (d) expanding the 220k switchyard; (e) constructing a 45 mile 220 kv double circuit line to the site of a new aluminum factory to be located at Jaigad; and (f) supplementing the transmission capacity toward Bombay. The demand for electricity in the Bombay-Poona area warrants substantial additions to generating capacity of the system serving this area as soon as possible. The completion of the second Stage of the Koyna development is the quickest and most economical method of providing this additional capacity.

P009623.project_abstract: The Purna Irrigation (State of Maharashtra) Project in India will provide financing for the irrigation of 152,000 acres along the left side of the Purna River Valley in India. This project will consist of a composite dam of Yeldari with a reservoir of 784,000 acre feet gross capacity, a re-regulating reservoir of 200,00 acre feet behind another composite dam at Sidheshwar, about 50 miles of concrete, or masonry, lined main canal and 250 miles of distributaries to irrigate 152,000 acres. The project will provide reliable water supply for the irrigations of 152,000 acres of land now dependent on rainfall for crops.

P009616.project_abstract: The Sone Irrigation (State of Bihar) Project in India will provide financing for the improvement of the water supply. This project will consist of the construction of a new barrage across the Sone River to replace the existing diversion weir, headworks and navigation channels located at the new barrage would be connected to the existing canal system by link canals, remodeling and extension of the existing irrigation system. The new structure will provide better regulation of river flow and head for water supply. The project will improve the water supply for 733,000 acres of crops presently irrigated each year and would make possible the irrigation of about 300,000 additional acres of crops.

P009617.project_abstract: The Fourth Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation Project in India will finance a loan to replenish its foreign exchange resources. This project will consist of the creation, expansion, and modernization of private industrial enterprises which will encourage private local, and foreign capital participation in their financing, and assist in the creation of a securities market. This project will provide economic expansion for the Indian capital market.

P009620.project_abstract: The Durgapur Power Extension project for India will provide a credit to the Government of India for the expansion of the Durgapur power station and associated transmission system of the Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC). The DVC is a semi-autonomous organization created in 1948 to carry out a unified scheme of development of the Damodar Valley in the States of Bihar and Bengal. This project follows three previous Bank loans to help with the development of the Damodar Valley by DVC. The components of the project are the construction of a 140 MW thermal generating plant and additional transmission facilities. The thermal plant is a hydrogen cooled turbo-generator and will be an extension of the existing Durgapur power station. It will be adjacent to the Durgapur steel plant, and will use coal middlings which are a waste product from an adjacent coal washing plant. The transmission system enhancements will include: a) transmission line construction comprising about 5 miles of 132 kv double circuit line and about 12 miles of 33 kv line; b) modifications and extension of substations at Durgapur, Bokaro, Chandrapura, Sindri, kalipahari, Ramgarh, Luchipur, Ramkanali, Burdwan, Oyaria, and Maithon; and c) construction of a central load dispatch and system control station at Maithon. The report notes that even with the additional capacity generated by this thermal plant, DVC will not be able to fully meet power demand in the area. This report finds the project to be sound and cost estimates to be reasonable. The DVC has agreed to adjust its rates to assure a return of at least 7 percent. It will employ a firm of chartered accountants, approved by the IDA, to assure an adequate return. This project is suitable as a basis of a credit to the Government of India which will in turn supply to the DVC the foreign exchange required for the project.

P009619.project_abstract: The Third Indian Iron and Steel Company Project in India will assist in financing the expansion and opening up of coal mines and the construction of coal transportation facilities. This project will consist of steel-making facilities at Burnpur, the installation of a 6-mile long feeder ropeway from Jitpur to Chasnalla, and a 32-mile long ropeway from Chasnalla to Burnpur. This project will provide the company with a steady supply of coking coal of satisfactory quality.

P009615.project_abstract: The Punjab Flood Protection and Drainage Project in India will provide financing for flood protection and surface drainage in the State of Punjab. This project consistsof construction of embankments and other flood protection works along the banks of Rivers Beas, Sutlej, Juina, Ghaggar and other rivers; the canalizing and training of choes and nallahs (torrents); the excavation of drainage channels and the construction of associated works such as syphons, culverts, bridges, regulators and tributary drains. This project will provide the prevention of flood damage to crops, buildings and transportation facilities, and of an increase in crop yields in areas given adequate surface drainage.

P009614.project_abstract: A substantial increase in agricultural productivity is one of the basic objectives of India's economic development. The proposed credit is to finance one half of the total cost to be incurred during the Third Plan of a project to irrigate about 225,000 acres of land in the State of Orissa. Part of the proposed credit, equivalent to $1,250,000 would finance the import of equipment. The balance of $6,750,000 would be applied to the local currency cost of the dam, canal system and ancillary works and would be disbursed on the basis of a percentage of total local currency expenditures as they are made over the period of the project's execution. Benefits in terms of higher yields, more reliable production and crop diversification will be substantial. Agricultural production will increase several times in value. With irrigation, double cropping will be undertaken on almost 40 percent of the land, and much higher yields will be obtained for rice, the dominant crop. A variety of new crops will be introduced into the area.

P009613.project_abstract: The Shetrunji Irrigation (State of Gujarat) Project in India will provide financing for the completion of the Shetrunji Irrigation Scheme. This project will include the construction of the main canals and distributaries, together with the necessary structures, and the construction of buildings for the operation and maintenance of the distribution system. The scheme would provide irrigation water to 86,000 acres of land, at present under dry farming, a wide variety of crops, predominantly cereals, would be grown. It will increase the value of agricultural production with a favorable gross farm benefit/investment ratio of about 40 percent. The benefits to farmers would be substantial and the project is economically fully justified.

P009622.project_abstract: The Sixth Railways Project in India will provide financing to make up part of the arrears in renewals and to increase transportation capacity. The project will consist of the acquisition of locomotives, rolling stock, and other equipment, construction of new lines as well as track doubling, rail and tie renewals, electrification of certain lines, bridge works, yard re-modeling, and other works. This project will meet the operational requirements for India's railways.

P009612.project_abstract: The Uttar Pradesh Tubewell Irrigation Project in India will provide financing for the irrigation of water to regions that have insufficient precipitation, which are not within reach of canal irrigation systems. This project will consist of 530 slotted-pipe wells, and 270 strainer wells, which will be drilled to an average depth of 300 to 400 feet, and have an average capacity of 1.5 cusec. It will be equipped with pumps driven by electric motors with power supplied from the State grid system. The general objectives of the program are to increase agricultural production in the State of Uttar Pradesh by providing irrigation water to regions that have insufficient precipitation and are not within the reach of canal irrigation systems. Economically, the project is very attractive and fully justified.

P009621.project_abstract: The Second Port of Calcutta Project in India will provided the financing for the maintenance of the River Hooghly and improvement of the Port of Calcutta. This project includes the purchase of four new dredgers to supplement the existing, the inadequate Commissioners for the Port of Calcutta(CPC) dredging fleet, as well as other vessels to be employed on river conservancy and operational duties. In King George's Dock, the western arm will be extended to provide holding space for four ships, and four dolphin berths for ships undergoing repairs. In Kidderpore Docks a water re-circulation scheme will eliminate the siltation problem in the docks, and the no. 2 swing bridge will be replaced. Additional cranes, fork lift trucks, tractors and trailers are to be provided as a modest addition to the mechanical-handling equipment of the port. This project will provide the means of maintaining a facility vital to the continued growth of the largest and most important economic region in India.

P009618.project_abstract: The Coal Production Project in India will provide financing for the private coal mining industry to expand its production through the import of equipment. This project will consist of spare parts, replacements, and equipment for the expansion of the existing mines. Coal is a basic element in the Indian economy, and must be counted on to play a predominant role in the future development of the country. Although the country has ample coal reserves, the average quality is low.

P009610.project_abstract: The Road Project for India will provide financing for construction and reconstruction of National Highways and Bombay Expressways. This project will consist of the procurement of the necessary equipment needed for the execution of the works under a technical, and economic study by foreign consultants of the traffic problems of downtown Bombay in connection with the expressways already under construction and the contemplated future expressways and highways in the area. This project will eliminate the major deficiencies in the National Highway system.

P009609.project_abstract: The Third Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation Project in India will finance a loan to replenish its foreign exchange resources in order to meet the growing demand of its customers for foreign exchange loans. This project will consist of the development of private industry in India by making available medium-term and long-term loans in foreign exchange, to encourage local and foreign private capital participation in such financing, to make equity investments and to assist in the expansion of the Indian capital market. The project was created to assist in the development of private industry in India, to encourage local and foreign private capital participation in its financing, and to assist in the expansion of the Indian capital market.

P009611.project_abstract: The Fifth Railway Project for India will finance a loan to execute the rehabilitation and improvement program. This project will consist of the procurement of locomotives, spare parts, other railway materials and equipment, and for services connected therewith. This project is essential to the economic development of India.

P009608.project_abstract: The Fourth Railway Project for India updates appraisals previously made in connections with loans made in July 1957 and September 1958 to help finance the Idian Railways' part of the Second Five-Year Plan. Theses appraisals were reported in TO143 and TO190 respectively. It is recommended that consideration be given to a loan of US $50 million equivalent for purchasing railways equipment, materials, and services. A term of twenty years, including a grace period of three years is recommended.

P009607.project_abstract: The Second Industrial Credit Project for India provides the Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation (ICICI) a second loan of $10 million to replenish its foreign exchange resources. The ICICI was created to assist in the development of private industry in India, to encourage local and foreign private capital participation in its financing , and to assist in the expansion of the Indian capital market. This report reviews the corporation's past performance, management and organization, and its investment program and financial prospects, as well as presenting the report's conclusions and recommendations.

P009604.project_abstract: This report covers an appraisal of the first stage of the Koyna Hydro-Electric Power project for India which will include; a transmission line to Bombay, and a transmission line south of the project to serve a number of small towns, villages, and their small industries. Stage I, now under construction, will have an installed capacity of 240 MW; Stage II will provide an additional 240 mw, and water storage for irrigation; Stage III will utilize the tailrace waters of the Stage II power plant and irrigation water, and it will add an additional 90 mw. The continually growing demand for power requires the provision of new generating capacity of the magnitude of Koyna and the development of this project is the most economical method of providing the power.

P009606.project_abstract: The Third Railways Project will provide loans to the Government of India to increase the capacity of the Indian Railways. Loans to the equivalent of $90 million were made by the Bank in July 1957 to help finance part of the Second Five-Year Plan. An appraisal was made in Report No. TO143. This is an update of the appraisal. Progress of the Railways' part of the Plan has been satisfactory, while other sectors of the Plan have fallen behind schedule. As a result the shortage of rail transport is less acute now than it was two years ago. The planned increase of capacity has been raised from 47 to 54 million tons, to bring the total freight capacity to 168 million tons by 1961. This is to be accomplished by an adjustment of rolling stock procurement to provide an additional 11,000 freight cars. Changes have been made in the Railways' Plan because of shortages of materials, foreign exchange problems, and rising prices. While these factors have caused shifts of emphasis and rephrasing of some works, and while the final investment in physical terms may be rather less than was planned, the Railways' program remains fundamentally sound.

P009605.project_abstract: This report covers an appraisal of a project for The Third Damodar Valley Power Expansion Project for India. The project will consist of a 150 UV thermal plant, three multipurpose dams, two hydroelectric installations totaling 100 MDW, a barrage and irrigation system, and transmission system facilities. A recent power survey shows that from 1959 until 1962 or 1963 DVC will not be able to run all of the requirements of its area. Additional power will be required primarily by new industries and a railroad electrification program which is included in India in the second five year plan.

P009599.project_abstract: This report is an appraisal of a project for the Modernization and Expansion of the Port of Madras in India. The project will reduce congestion by speeding up the turn round of ships, lower the cost of handling cargo in the port, and increase the overall operating efficiency. Furthermore, it will result in a considerable increase in the port's capacity to handle general cargo, which is necessary to meet the growth in traffic expected during the next ten years. At the end of the construction period, there will still be sufficient reserve capacity in the port to avoid the threat of congestion during peak periods.

P009598.project_abstract: This report covers an appraisal of a project for the Rehabilitation and Improvement of the Port of Calcutta, in India. The project consists of the conversion of several old King Georgets dock berths into three new general cargo berths with transit sheds, ore oil, berth and one laying-up berth. Several berths in Kidderpore dock will also be improved, and the quay walls in twelve other berths reconditioned and strengthened. Electric cranes and lifts, mechanical cargo-handling equipment, two floating cranes, and the existing railroad will be improved along with additional railway equipment acquired. This project will provide improvement of existing equipment which has passed its useful economic life, and improve existing facilities.

P009597.project_abstract: The Second Tata Iron and Steel Project will finance a loan to provide the cost of goods and equipment (including spare parts), supplies and services needed for the Project, which consists of the expansion and modernization of Jamshedpur, which will be designed to increase their capacity to about 2,000,000 long tons of steel ingots and 1,500,000 tons of semi-finished and finished steel products. The development of the coal and iron mines, and other related and ancillary works, are also included. India's demand for steel is growing rapidly, and any increase in domestic supplies will bring important savings in foreign exchange. The expansion of the iron and steel industry will therefore be of considerable benefit to the economy as a whole.

P009603.project_abstract: The Second Railway Project is principally directed to increasing the capacity of the railways to handle additional traffic. Its most important elements are the acquisition of new rolling stock, the doubling of main-line tracks, improvement in yards, and new signalling. A beginning is made on dieselization of some main-line services, and a further important development in motive power is electrification of certain very high density passenger and freight traffic areas.

P009602.project_abstract: The Second Railway Project is principally directed to increasing the capacity of the railways to handle additional traffic. Its most important elements are the acquisition of new rolling stock, the doubling of main-line tracks, improvement in yards, and new signalling. A beginning is made on dieselization of some main-line services, and a further important development in motive power is electrification of certain very high density passenger and freight traffic areas.

P009601.project_abstract: The Second Railway Project is principally directed to increasing the capacity of the railways to handle additional traffic. Its most important elements are the acquisition of new rolling stock, the doubling of main-line tracks, improvement in yards, and new signalling. A beginning is made on dieselization of some main-line services, and a further important development in motive power is electrification of certain very high density passenger and freight traffic areas.

P009600.project_abstract: The Second Railway Project is principally directed to increasing the capacity of the railways to handle additional traffic. Its most important elements are the acquisition of new rolling stock, the doubling of main-line tracks, improvement in yards, and new signalling. A beginning is made on dieselization of some main-line services, and a further important development in motive power is electrification of certain very high density passenger and freight traffic areas.

P009595.project_abstract: The Trombay Thermal Power Station Expansion Project provides finance for the addition of a third thermal generating unit, similar in characteristics to the two units now nearing completion, in the Trombay station located on the northeast shore of Bombay harbor. The unit will have a maximum capacity of 62,500 kw in a 50 cycle turbo-generator supplied with steam from a 6000,000 lb/hr boiler. Operation will be at 1250 lb per square inch pressure and at 950 degrees temperature. The plant will be equipped with coal crushing and handling equipment and will primarily use domestic coal from Central India. It will also be equipped to burn fuel oil and by-products from the adjacent Stanvac oil refinery. The latter fuel is now used in the original plant. The project is estimated to cost the equivalent of 14 million. The Bank has been requested to finance the foreign exchange cost, estimated at the equivalent of $9.8 million inclusive of interest during construction. The loan will be for a period of 18 years including a grace period on amortization payments of approximately 3 years. The project, which should be completed in April 1960, will help meet a continuing shortage of power which is particularly acute in the Bombay area pending construction of a large hydro development at Koyna.

P009596.project_abstract: The Air India Jet Project will provide a loan to Air India, the Indian-flag carrier on world routes. The project includes the purchase of three jets powered by 12 original engines; radio, galley, and other aircraft auxiliaries; 9 spare engines; other initial spares and stores; some overhaul facilities, a test cell and other special equipment; and a flight simulator. Air India needs more aircraft to cope with growing traffic, and might fail to hold its share of the business unless it acquires jets. For these reasons, Air India has just ordered for early 1960 delivery, three Boeing 707 jets of the 420 model which will be powered by four Rolls-Royce Conway engines each. These three planes have the same service potential, roughly 60 million capacity ton miles a year, as ten Super-Constellations. Air India will have sufficient equipment by 1960/61 for flying 120 million capacity ton miles a year compared with 42 million actually flown in 2956/57.

P009594.project_abstract: The Second Indian Iron and Steel Company Expansion Project for India will finance a project to expand the company's steel rolling capacity. The Tata Iron and Steel Company, Limited (TISCO) is engaged in an expansion program primarily designed to increase its capacity to produce steel ingots from 1.1 million tons to two million tons, and its capacity to produce saleable steel from 780,000 to 1.5 million tons per annum. This expansion program consists of four parts: a modernization and expansion program (known as MEP), a program of further expansion (known as the Two Million Ton Program, or TMTP) designed to increase annual capacity to two million tons of ingots and 1.5 million tons of saleable products. This project is of high priority, and the potential benefits are considerable. The increase in output will provide a substantial addition to the amount of domestic steel available to meet the needs of the second five year plan, at a cost greatly below that of imported steel.

P009593.project_abstract: The Tata Iron and Steel Company Expansion and Modernization Project will provide the necessary raw materials which will make it possible to produce steel in India at a very low cost. This expansion program consists of four parts: A modernization, and expansion program (known as "MEP'), a program of further expansion (known as the two Million Ton Program or "TMTP'"), designed to increase annual capacity to 2 million tons of ingots and 1.5 million tons of saleable products. The Tata Iron and Steel Co., Ltd. (TISCO) is engaged in an expansion program primarily designed to increase its capacity to produce steel ingots from 1.1 million tons to 2 million tons, and its capacity to produce saleable steel from 780,000 to 1.5 million tons per annum. This project is of high priority, and benefits are very great. The increase in output will provide an important addition to the amount of domestic steel available to meet the needs of India.

P009591.project_abstract: The Second Loan Administration Report for India is a continuation of L162, and will finance a loan which will provide reconstruction for India. This project will consist of railway rehabilitation, agricultural machinery, Bokaro thermal plant, expansion of iron and steel productive capacity, electric power development, flood control, irrigation, and industrial credit and investment This project will provide further improvement for India's economy.

P009592.project_abstract: The Second Loan Administration Report for India is a continuation of L162, and will finance a loan which will provide reconstruction for India. This project will consist of railway rehabilitation, agricultural machinery, Bokaro thermal plant, expansion of iron and steel productive capacity, electric power development, flood control, irrigation, and industrial credit and investment This project will provide further improvement for India's economy.

P502499.project_abstract: The proposed Surat Resilience Enhancement Project (SREP) is expected to support the Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) and the Tapi River Front Development Corporation Limited (TRFDCL) in implementing the Tapi Riverfront Rejuvenation Plan (TRRP) within the broader context of mainstreaming resilience in municipal operations and increasing resilience of the city to extreme flood and heat events, ensuring sustainability of resilient infrastructure development through leverage of own source revenues including land value capture mechanisms, achieving economic rejuvenation of the riverfront area, and integrating nature-based and green infrastructure solutions into the riverfront development. The TRRP is seeking to bend the curve by taking a resilience approach to riverfront development instead of a simple placemaking approach which is common to riverfront development projects in India. SMC is updating its draft conceptual master plan for the TRRP spread along 33.6 km on each side of Tapi river between the Kathore Bridge to a proposed barrage downstream of Singanpore wier. TRRP is expected to construct new embankments where required as well as inspect and strengthen existing embankments and dykes on the riverfront while making space available for increased economic, recreational and cultural activities. These activities are proposed to be implemented in two phases: Phase I, an up to10 km river stretch along both banks between the proposed barrage (connecting Rundh and Bhata) and the Singanpore weir; and Phase II, the remaining 23.6 km river stretch along both banks upstream from the Singanpore weir to the Kathore bridge. Through these interventions, the SMC expects to reduce the city’s flooding risks and beautify the cityscape to induce recreational, tourism and commercial activities, as well as prevent saltwater intrusion through the construction of the proposed Barrage (to be financed by SMC separately, i.e. non-World Bank financing). The proposed SREP Project will implement Phase I of the TRRP, and intends to set the technical, quality, legal, aesthetic, and E&S practices benchmarks for the following phase to follow, whether or not this is financed by the World Bank.The SREP will bring in international good practices in urban riverfront development and resilient infrastructure service delivery including: (i) interventions needed to make “room for the river”, while ensuring the livelihood of residents; (ii) incorporating shared spaces along the riverbanks for the river and for people, guided by ecological thinking; (iii) an inclusive development approach with proactive and continuous stakeholder engagement to define the multiple uses of spaces; as well as (iv) a sustainable financial and operational model to help the SMC, including through TRFDCL, manage its infrastructure assets and sustain effective and efficient service delivery in the long run. Public spaces along the river will be treated as a city public good and will get a careful, site and community specific programming and participatory design, that attends to city needs and cultural practices. The output of the investments will not only enhance the flood risk management capacity of the city and improve the living conditions of the residents, but also enhance economic development opportunities for both the public and the private sectors.The SREP suggests interventions under three complementary pillars. The 'resilience pillar' focuses on delivery of the TRRP as explained above. The 'institutions pillar' focuses on institutionalizing climate resilience actions in SMC including assigning one of the existing special implementation units called 'Cells' in SMC as the 'Climate Action Unit' (CAU) for quality assurance of all large investment projects and sectoral strategies and coordinating all climate resilience related matters. The CAU will serve as the anchor and nerve center for advancing SMC’s ambition of becoming the first ‘Green Municipal Corporation’ of India. The 'finance pillar' focuses on strengthening the investment planning and financial management systems, upgrading existing asset management MIS, upgrading procedures for disposition of monetizable assets, supporting SMC in undertaking pilot land monetization transactions especially focusing on land parcels falling within the TRRP, strengthening systems and procedures for management of unused and underused real estate, and building SMC’s technical capacity to manage the new real estate portfolio management system, in addition to looking at avenues for leveraging other land value capture tools through strengthening of real estate-based fees and policies including floor space index (FSI) and transferrable development rights (TDR). The three pillars will be supplemented by project management support and capacity augmentation. The four proposed components of SREP will be: Component 1: Resilient Urban Infrastructure Investments- C1.1: Tapi riverfront development investments proposed in Phase I of the TRRP, including: (i) flood risk control and resilience enhancement through a combination of green infrastructure (nature-based solutions) and grey infrastructure (engineered solutions and embankments) to arrive at a solution that achieves a harmonious balance between interventions on flood protection, urban ecology and urban riverfront amenity provision; (ii) public space enhancement and land redevelopment to increase the amenities and economic opportunities for the residents and business owners along the riverfront; and (iii) enhancement of cultural heritage assets and infrastructure along the riverfront that promote cultural tourism.- C1.2: Select supplementary resilient infrastructure investments, including a drainage interceptor project to rehabilitate the drainage outfall system along Tapi river, and small additional essential investments not proposed under TRRP such as access roads/mobility, etc. Component 2: Institutional Strengthening on Resilience Planning - C1.1: Institutional resilience and climate mainstreaming including setting-up and operationalization of the Climate Action Unit which would lead mainstreaming of climate and resilience actions in SMC including through translation of the existing second-generation climate strategy into a costed Climate Action Plan (CAP), mainstreaming disaster and climate resilience in all large projects of SMC, initiating green budgeting, setting up green accounting codes, exploring green financing through green municipal bonds and PPPs, fostering inter- and intra-departmental coordination, capacity building of SMC staff, developing a one-city one-map approach that ensures coordination between all developmental projects of SMC, among others. - C1.2: Operationalizing an integrated multi-hazard early warning system (EWS) and emergency response system (ERS) including modernization of the Hydromet monitoring network, including the development of a concept of operation (CONOPS) for key stakeholders, modernization in current EWS and ERS towards feeding into development of a multi-hazard EWS and ERS defining the development of a hydrological-hydraulic model for the forecasting, guidance and dissemination on flood warning in Surat as well as other hazards such as urban heat, vector borne pandemics, etc., integration with SMC's Command and Control Center (CCC) towards possible hosting of the integrated multi-hazard EWS and ERS, improve early warning dissemination systems, capacity building of SMC for disaster preparedness and response, among others. Component 3: Municipal Finance Improvement - C3.1: Enhancing overall performance on municipal finance of SMC, including technical assistance to help the SMC improve its capacity, systems, and practices in financial management, including towards integrating climate strategies, plans, and policies in fiscal and public financial management, as well as climate budget tagging for resilient urban development investments.- C2.2: Improving revenue performance of the SMC, thr

P181020.project_abstract: Component 1: Investments in an accessible and sustainable Metrorail system. This component will finance: a) Metro rail infrastructure. Construction of approximately 28.50 km of elevated metro line in Gurugram, with 27 metro stations, depot, procurement & installation of rolling stock, electric, telecommunication, signaling, and control systems;  b) Multi-modal integration with other public transit systems; and c) Infrastructure for first and last mile connectivity including bus routing, bike sharing facilities and improvement in public spaces. Component 2: Promoting Transit Oriented Development (TOD) and integrated urban development in the catchment area of the metro line. This component will finance: a) Technical assistance to policies, planning and regulatory framework for TOD and integrated urban development strategy. b) Identification of prioritized resilient infrastructure in the catchment area for investment planning; and c) Pilot TOD complex development at/around two selected stations including planning, design, and implementation.Component 3: Technical assistance and capacity building to the key transport and urban development institutions. This component will finance: a) Technical support to inclusive and green infrastructure planning and design;b) Analytical activities for identification of innovative financing instruments for the metro system; c) Technical assistance for citizen engagement and gender inclusion; andd) Project management and operation.

P180672.project_abstract: The proposed operation will support: (i) reconstruction, rehabilitation, improvement of selected climate-resilient hill  roads in Dima Hasao, Karbi Anglong, and west Karbi Anglong districts; (ii) developing agricultural supply chain for a cluster of roadside tribal communities and promoting market-driven and climate-resilient agriculture; (iii) developing green and efficient rural freight and public transportation system; and (iv) building multi-modal transport network resilience and early warning system. The hill roads project will integrate the tribal communities with the economy of Assam and the sub region by  improving the resilience of road connectivity and the efficiency of the agricultural and  women tribal community households textile and handicraft producers supply chain. The project will also develop resilience enhancing instruments, establish early warning system (EWS) and emergency response system during disaster events, and strengthen institutional capacity to manage disaster prone roads.
P180672.project_name: Assam Disaster Resilient Hill Roads Development Project

P179725.project_abstract: The proposed National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project Phase III will, while partly continuing the cyclone preparedness and emergency management agenda targeted under phases I and II, shift the program’s focus from life-saving interventions to systemic resilience to disasters and extreme events amidst increasing climatic changes. NCRMP III will serve as a knowledge project by developing the analytical underpinnings to better understand and inform future efforts to enhance systemic resilience to climate change in coastal areas. First, the project will establish a knowledge platform on coastal resilience to integrate ongoing approaches and experiences and identify missing pieces of the agenda, with a focus on potential climate impacts. This platform will enable joint learning across coastal states and benchmarking of global best practices and lessons learned from Bank projects. Second, the project will analyze important biophysical and socioeconomic trends to provide empirical evidence on priority interventions and investments for next-generation coastal resilience. Third, the project will undertake action-oriented analytics in themes emerging from the experience of NCRMP II. Within a select number of low-lying coastal cities, the project will develop master drainage plans to address current and future drainage needs in light of amplified urban flooding risks posed by climate change. The project will assess saline embankments in coastal India to enable the development of a raised and strengthened embankment system to withstand the impact of cyclones. Lastly, the project will identify the most critical and exposed critical infrastructure assets, with a focus on power sector and lightning risk mitigation needs, as candidates for the strengthening of infrastructure to catalyze long-term growth and enhance the adaptive capacity of coastal communities to climate change and sea level rise.

P179548.project_abstract: The proposed project aims to improve landscape management to enhance ecosystem services and economic benefits for the forest-dependent communities in Tripura. More specifically, the project will strengthen the capacities of the state government and local actors to restore forest landscapes by introducing a landscape approach and helping utilize technological solutions. Through the proposed project, the degraded forest landscapes will be restored by implementing community-led integrated forest landscape and natural resource management plans in the selected areas in support of improved ecosystem services, such as water availability, soil conservation, and wildlife habitat protection, among others. The improved forest ecosystem will contribute to increased carbon sequestration and climate resilience and adaptive capacities of the communities. The project also aims at creating sustainable forest-based and NTFP livelihoods by facilitating value chain improvement and market linkages. As a direct contribution to income generating opportunities, the project will forge new employment avenues such as and strengthening existing and supporting the establishment of new value chains for NTFPs and HVFPs such as Bamboo and Agarwood, and ecotourism/nature-based tourism. For enhancing NTFP market linkages, the project will conduct training and capacity building for the collection and producer groups, forest institutions, NTFP traders, MSMEs, etc. and organize events to bring buyers and sellers together. Finally, the project will strengthen the functional and technical capacities of state institutions for improved landscape governance and disaster risk prevention by introducing new technology on forest monitoring and value chain management, while facilitating collaborative landscape management with the local actors. Other interventions aimed at the inclusion of tribal population, gender empowerment, and vocational development for women and youth will be prioritized during project preparation and implementation.
P179548.project_name: Enhancing Landscape and Ecosystem Management - Tripura

P179323.project_abstract: The development objective of the Electric Vehicle Operations and Lending for a Vibrant Ecosystem (EVOLVE) is to foster the transition to sustainable electric vehicles in the two and three-wheeler segments. The Project will take a three-pronged approach to address current challenges. First, it will address the key market failure underlying the lack of access to affordable commercial financing for e-2/3Ws and associated charging infrastructure through a risk-sharing program (RSP), which will offer credit-enhancement and on-lending products to a diverse range of participating financial institutions (PFIs). End borrowers are expected to include, inter alia, micro, small and medium enterprises, leasing companies, fleet operators, aggregators, and charging-as-a-service (“CaaS”) and battery-as-a-service (“BaaS”) businesses. Micro enterprises include individual, driver cum owners with mandatory Udyam Aadhar registration, a unique registration mechanism for MSMEs. PFIs will offer reduced interest cost and lend more actively to women borrowers. EVOLVE will systematically embed and test de-risking measures to improve the ability of the PFIs to appraise and price risks, and build a track record in e-2/3W lending, thereby moving towards a self-sustaining EV financing ecosystem. Second, EVOLVE will contribute to addressing barriers and fostering key enablers by leveraging the large-scale data generated from the EVs financed under EVOLVE RSP to help policy makers in framing the EV transition, help consumers make informed decisions about switching to EVs, and mitigate lenders’ concerns over lending to EVs, and by building the capacity of the Program Manager and PFIs. EVOLVE will also contribute to the knowledge base in key areas of sustainability such as RE integration, effective lifecycle management of batteries, and facilitation of women’s access to financing to promote vehicle ownership, and women’s labor force participation associated with e-2/3Ws. Lastly, EVOLVE will provide the scale necessary to make the aggregation of carbon credits viable, which could monetize GHG emissions reductions, a key positive externality of EVs. EVOLVE would be designed with an open architecture, to allow other financing agencies and donors with specific interests to benefit from its structure. SIDBI, a pan-India financial institution, will perform the role of ‘Program Manager’ at the national level, and establish and implement the EVOLVE RSP.
P179323.borrower: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
P179323.impagency: Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
P179323.project_name: Electric Vehicle Operations and Lending for a Vibrant Ecosystem

P178967.project_abstract: The goal of the program is to promote the well-being and empowerment of adolescents and to strengthen their productivity and resilience so that they can contribute fully to the sustainable economic growth of the state. The program will strengthen the capability of the State of Meghalaya to empower adolescent boys and girls, aged 9 to 19, through multi-sectoral interventions (education/skills/counselling) that can strengthen their human capital, and support their transition from school to productive work. The program would support strengthening adolescents' life skills, physical and reproductive health, and career aspirations.Component 1.  Learning Mission, Life Skills, and Career Preparation in Schools: This component will focus on improving human capital outcomes for adolescents in upper primary (grades 6-8), secondary (grades 9-10), and higher secondary (grades 11-12) government and government-aided schools in the state. Component 2: Community Interventions and pathways for out-of-school adolescents: This component will focus on improving human capital outcomes for out of school adolescents and creating an enabling environment for them through active engagement and capability building of their parents, community members, and frontline workers. It will also support setting up of a “Hub and Spoke Model” of community-based service delivery through the network of Community Clubs (located at the level of cluster of villages) and Youth Centres (located at Block levels). Component 3: State Capability and Program Management: This component will focus on strengthening the institutional capacity of the state for improved coordination, governance, and outreach, set up Youth Centres as Block level hubs for adolescents and youth, and support improved management of data, and day to operation and management of the project. This component will also support adolescent girls in completing the secondary education cycle through academic counselling, development of a multisectoral competency and wellbeing framework, and facilitating safe spaces for young girls. Component 4: Contingent Emergency Response Component (CERC): This component will support an immediate response to an eligible crisis or emergency, as needed.
P178967.project_name: Meghalaya Multisectoral Project for Adolescent Wellbeing, Empowerment and Resilience (MPOWER)

P178571.project_name: Strengthening Teaching-Learning and Results for States – Learning Enhancement and Acceleration during Pandemic (LEAP) program

P178239.project_abstract: The proposed project will address key gaps and deficiencies in the dairy sector in focus states in India and support the sector’s transformation towards increased productivity, resilience, and profitability. By doing so, it will contribute to key aspects of the GoI and the Bank’s CPF strategic objectives related to faster and broader agriculture sector growth and inclusive development. The project will also work closely with the pipeline project under development – Animal Health System Support for Improved One Health (AHSSOH) – to enhance animal health management. Farmers have limited access to the organized milk processing sector. Only about 36 percent of the marketable surplus is estimated to be sold to the organized sector. Small producers, who account for 70 percent of milk production, are particularly affected. Also, milk processed and marketed by the organized sector is safer and less likely to be contaminated, which offers health and food safety benefits. In addition to the marketing and food safety challenges Productivity is low mainly due to poor nutrition, health, the low genetic potential for milk production, and the near absence of well-run genetic improvement programs. Animal nutrition is undermined not only by feed and fodder scarcity but also lack of farmers‟ knowledge on how to better use existing feed resources. There is little extension advice available to farmers about improved animal feeding practices.The project will help to increase milk production by improving nutrition and enhancing farmers' knowledge on how to use better existing feed resources and optimal use of feed and fodder. This would be achieved through support to extensive training of dairy farmers and doorstep delivery of ration advisory services, integrated with veterinary support, together with convergence with the DAHD programme. The project will raise farmers' ‟awareness” about the importance of good quality milk and build their capacity for hygienic milk production, collection and sale. The collective sale will strengthen farmers‟ negotiating power and reduce transaction costs for such a highly perishable commodity.The project recognizes the role of an enabling policy and regulatory environment to support the intended investments. Consequently, project investments would be supported in those states that commit to certain time-bound actions onwards a more enabling policy environment.
P178239.impagency: Department of Animal Husbandry and Dairying,National Dairy Development Board

P177964.project_abstract: The Project will enhance green, resilient, inclusive, developmentally-efficient and safe urban mobility in the CMA with demonstration in selected areas, through the following three components: --> Component 1: Integrated land-use and transport planning, and accelerated implementation with private sector participation. This component will leverage the unique opportunities offered by the simultaneous development of the TMP and CMP, to promote land use - transport integration through TOD principles at different scales across the CMA. The component will also support the efficient implementation of these plans with technical assistance to encourage private sector participation. --> Component 2: Integrated planning and delivery of infrastructure projects supported by digital solutions. This component will focus on infrastructure interventions to encourage modal shifts to public transport and promote walkability and access. The component will also support the development and deployment of digital tools to induce a step change in the efficiency of end-to-end planning, delivery, and management of infrastructure. --> Component 3: Safe and inclusive urban mobility systems. This component will make urban mobility infrastructure and systems in Chennai safe and inclusive for all users, particularly women.

P177844.project_abstract: The World Bank financed PforR Program supports a portion of the Government Program (Revamped Reform-linked Result-based Distribution Sector Scheme (RDSS)) and will focus on policy and structural reforms, and limited investments (metering and associated ICT systems only) that are essential to achieve the financial sustainability and operational efficiency of state-owned Discoms. While the government program covers all public Discoms across the country, the proposed PforR Program targets two states (Madhya Pradesh and Rajasthan) who have demonstrated willingness to undertake deeper reforms. Further, the World Bank PforR program will be implemented by REC Ltd (a financial intermediary), which is also the nodal agency of the RDSS scheme. The proposed operation also includes a Technical Assistance or TA (as an IPF component) for implementation support and capacity building of Discoms in the participating states to implement the reforms. The TA component will include consultancy support for: (i) Resource adequacy planning and implementing power procurement optimization tool, (ii) institutionalizing the process for preparation and updation of financial turnaround plan of Discoms, (iii) Program implementation for pilots in Direct Benefit Transfer of Subsidy, (iv) implementation of grid modernization by adoption of Information Technology (IT)/ Operational Technology (OT) systems, and (v) capacity building and knowledge exchange with other national and international utilities. This component will also be implemented by REC Ltd using World Bank’s IPF instrument.
P177844.project_name: Program for Electricity Distribution Sector Reforms in India

P177799.project_abstract: The proposed GRCP-Surat Project will support the Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) in addressing key institutional, financial, and service delivery constraints to strengthen the resilience and sustainability in Surat in line with the urban sector partnership framework under the Gujarat Resilient Cities Partnership (GRCP). In response to the climate resilience challenges that Surat faces, Surat Municipal Corporation (SMC) has proposed to implement a Tapi Riverfront Redevelopment Project (TRRP), led by the Tapi Riverfront Development Corporation Limited (TRFDCL), with the aim to improve the living conditions and access to services, flood risk management, and economic development opportunities along the urban banks of Tapi River. These activities are proposed to be implemented in two phases: Phase I, an around 10 km river stretch along both banks between the proposed barrage (connecting Rundh and Bhata) and the upstrem existing Singanpor weir; and Phase II, the remianing 23 km river stretch along both banks upstream from the Singanpor weir to the Kathore bridge. Public spaces along the river will be treated as a city public good and will get a careful, site and community specific programming and participatory design, that attends to neighborhood needs and cultural practices. The output of the investments will not only enhance the flood risk management capacity of the city and improve the living conditions of the residents, but also enhance economic development opportunities for both the public and the private sectors. To this end, the project comprises the following components: Component 1: Institutional Strengthening on Resilience Planning  - C1.1: Capacity building for SMC: (i) technical assistance for an integrated water basin management for the Tapi River; and (vi) integration of updated mobility plan with the urban development plan.- C1.2: Strengthening of the TRFDCL: (i) strengthening the institutional and governance structure of the TRFDCL; (ii) developing a capital structure and a revenue model to ensure effective, efficient, and sustainable implementation of the TRRP; and (iii) strengthening the operational systems of the TRFDCL.Component 2: Municipal Finance Improvement - C2.1: Enhancing overall performance on municipal finance of SMC, including technical assistance to help the SMC improve its capacity, systems, and practices in financial management, including towards integrating climate strategies, plans, and policies in fiscal and public financial management, as well as climate budget tagging for resilient urban development investments.- C2.2: Improving revenue performance of the SMC, through: (i) updating the tax base by using GIS-based surveys, geotagging, etc. and improving collection efficiency; (ii) improvements and rehabilitation of drainage and sanitation infrastructure investments to improve water conservation and river pollution control; (iii) public space enhancement and land redevelopment to increase the amenities and economic opportunities for the residents and business owners along the riverfront.- C3.2: Selected supplementary resilient infrastructure investments, namely, small additional investments that are essential, but are currently not proposed under the TRRP, such as additional drainage connections, access roads/mobility, etc.Component 4: Project Management and Operation, including the operational cost for implementing project activities, development, and implementation of environment and social (E&S) instruments, project reporting, monitoring and evaluation, as well as a project management consultancy, if needed.Under Component 3, the proposed Project will aim at building a “Safer Surat”. Implementation of this component will aim at minimizing damages during times of flooding resulting in less risk to people and infrastructure, and ensuring that there is ample room for flooding and river adjustment to occur where the opportunity may exist. It also means that flood recovery may be less expensive and may get people back on their feet more quickly than in past flood events, and becomes a way of helping people and communities live with and plan for flooding. P177666.project_abstract: The Delhi-Gurugram-SNB RRTS project will connect with the Delhi-Ghaziabad-Meerut RRTS Corridor at Sarai Kale Khan Station through seamless passenger movement between the two corridors. A high-speed (180km/h design speed) and high-frequency (5 min headway), rapid transit rail system (RRTS) will be implemented and will promote regional connectivity within the SNB urban complex in Rajasthan, Ghaziabad and Meerut in Uttar Pradesh State, and Rewari, Dharuhera, Gurugram in Haryana State, through Delhi. In addition to this, the project will support the development of gender and disability-inclusive diagnosis and design; as well as support to increase the financial sustainability and scalability of the RRTS, through TOD, multimodal integration, and asset monetization strategies.The total length of the entire Delhi-Gurugram-SNB RRTS Corridor is 106.5 km, of which 35.94 km will be underground, and 70.56 km will be elevated. Of the 70.56 km elevated portion of the proposed alignment, 58 km of the length is mainly planned over the road medians of old Delhi-Gurugram Road, Sector-17 Road in Gurugram and Right of Way of NH-48 up to SNB (Rajasthan State Border). With 11 elevated and 5 underground stations, the alignment will have a total of 16 stations between Sarai Kale Khan and SNB. The length of proposed route passing through Delhi will be 22.08 km (21.86 km underground, and 0.22 km elevated), 82.48 km (14.08km underground, 68.40km elevated) in Haryana and 1.94 km (elevated) in Rajasthan.The operation is proposed as IPFs (as part of MPA) to support implementing RRTS (civil works, tracks, systems, rolling stock), as well as consultancy and TA for designing climate-informed and gender-inclusive designs, safety audit, TOD and multimodal integration under all three components of the proposed MPA. NCRTC has already initiated preconstruction activities and has tendered out the execution of enabling civil works and works related to shifting of utilities such as water pipeline, electric lines, storm water drain, sewer line, gas pipelines, road widening works, etc. and associated electrical & telecom works, planning and design consultancies for depots, elevated and underground stations, and geotechnical investigations in multiple locations.

P174830.project_abstract: The envisioned MPA Program seeks to enhance institutional capacities and mechanisms for earthquake risk management at national andstate-levels, including management of disease outbreaks, and strengthen critical public infrastructure for earthquake resistance inhigh to very high-risk seismic zones in India. Given the (i) multiplicity of stakeholders and varying capacities across 14 highseismic risk States; (ii) the need for promoting long-term seismic risk management planning at the national scale; and (iii) theongoing exponential increase in risk due to unplanned urbanization, the project proposes a multi-phased programmatic approach. Asuite of instruments and program components are proposed under three engagement areas: Institutional and Policy Reforms,Investments for Demonstration Effect, and Knowledge and Capacities Pool. Further, it is envisioned that these are underpinned by astrong learning agenda, a platform approach, and crowding-in financial resources.

P009668.project_abstract: The project, which forms part of the Indian Fourth Five-Year Plan (1969-74), would provide some of the transport services required by increasing oil refinery capacity and by rapidly increasing consumption of refined products. The project consists of: (i) the purchase of four crude oil tankers in the 80,000 dwt class for use between the Persian Gulf and Haldia, and (ii) the purchase of two refined oil products tankers in the 20,000 dwt class for the import, export and coastal distribution of refined petroleum products. In addition, shore facilities will be improved and pollution-control equipment installed at Haldia, Cochin and other oil-handling ports. One or more crude oil transfer vessels totalling about 16,000 dwt for use at Haldia will also be provided.

P009667.project_abstract: Sweden and the Association would jointly finance the total project cost, pari-passu, on a one-to-two ratio. Sweden would thus participate with the equivalent of US$10.6 million and the Association would extend a credit of US$21.2 million equivalent. In broad terms, the joint-financing arrangement would cover expenditures under the project for three main purposes, namely: (a) investments in plant (buildings, furniture, equipment, vehicles) to complete and supplement the GOI pattern in project areas; (b) the nutrition component; and (c) incremental recurrent costs for the innovative parts of the project (the intensive rural component and the Population Centers).
